title: Offline Reinforcement Learning as One Big Sequence Modeling Problem
layout_note: Three horizontal bands stacked vertically: an input token row at the bottom, one full-width model bar in the middle, and an output token row at the top. The output row repeats the input sequence shifted one slot to the left, so each column pairs an input token with the next token; arrows are drawn only in columns where a box sits on that side.
grouping: No containers or background panels; grouping is by colour family only. State tokens are blue, action tokens salmon, the reward token orange, and same-type tokens sit in contiguous runs. Ellipses inside a run are three small filled dots tinted with that run's colour (blue between state tokens and at both row ends, salmon between action tokens).
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with a generous corner radius and a thin black outline, pastel fills, no shadows or 3-D. Each token is a near-square tile holding a bold math symbol with sub/superscripts. The model is a single wide white rounded bar with the same thin black outline spanning the full row width. Connectors are short thin black vertical arrows with small arrowheads.
proposed_highlight: The model is the only worded element: a plain white full-width bar with its name in bold serif centred inside. The paper's idea (states, actions and rewards as one sequence) is carried by the colour-coded token rows rather than by any emphasis on the model box; there is no legend, the bold letters s, a, r decode the colours.
lesson: Autoregressive next-token prediction is shown by placing the same colour-coded token row below and above one wide model bar with the upper row shifted one slot left, so the offset reads without a label.
notes: Token labels are typeset math symbols (state dimensions 1..N, action dimensions 1..M, reward, then the next state's first dimension in the output row). Single-row-height figure with a wide aspect; the crop (made by hand) includes an empty margin below the bottom row, which counts toward the measured whitespace. Venue and year read from the PDF's first-page footer.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: offline RL as sequence modelling of discretised trajectories

core.what: a trajectory is drawn as one flat row of per-dimension tokens - state dimensions s_t^1 ... s_t^N in blue, action dimensions a_t^1 ... a_t^M in red, reward r_t in orange - entering a single wide Trajectory Transformer box from below, and the same row leaves above shifted one position left, i.e. next-token prediction

relations.form: token boxes in one horizontal line in trajectory order (state dims, action dims, reward, next state), with coloured dots marking elided runs
the output row is the input row shifted by one token (input starts s_t^1, output starts s_t^2 and ends with s_{t+1}^1), every input arrow directly below the token it predicts
one wide rounded box spans the whole row, each input token entering it by a short vertical arrow and each output leaving by one

channels.colour: fill = token type: blue = state dimension, red = action dimension, orange = reward; the ellipsis dots take the colour of the elided tokens - one meaning
channels.shape: rounded squares = tokens; one long rounded rectangle = the model

quality.strengths: the two ideas - treating each state and action dimension as its own token, and predicting the next token - are both geometry: the row is visibly cut per dimension and the output row is shifted one slot against the input; colour is a single type code that also tints the elisions; all lines are short and straight
quality.weaknesses: the discretisation of continuous values into tokens and the causal mask are not shown, and the transformer is an empty box; the per-dimension superscripts are small, so the shift has to be read from the labels rather than from a visual offset in the boxes, which are aligned in the same columns

insights.structure: Three horizontal bands: an input token row at the bottom, one full-width 'Trajectory Transformer' bar in the middle, and the output token row at the top shifted one slot left.
insights.data: Each token is a rounded tile holding a bold math symbol: blue for state dimensions s_t^i, salmon for action dimensions a_t^j, orange for reward r_t; runs are elided by three dots tinted in the run's colour.
insights.emphasis: The shift of the output row by one token makes next-token prediction visible without any text; colour families separate state, action and reward.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: short black arrows from each input tile up into the bar and from the bar up to each output tile.
insights.avoid: Arrows are drawn only in columns that hold a tile on that side, so a few columns look disconnected; there is no causal-mask cue.

arrangement.units: one composition: input token row, model bar, output token row; no frames
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of coloured token tiles with math symbols
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (implied by shifted output row)
